text:
Deloitte Data Engineer interviews don’t reject you for syntax.
 They reject you for shallow thinking.
After going through real Deloitte Data Engineer interview questions (0–4 YOE), one thing is very clear 👇
They don’t ask:
 ❌ “What is PySpark?”
They ask:
 ✅ “How would you design this in the real world?”
Here’s what Deloitte actually tests 👇
🔹 SQL window functions — second highest, duplicates, ranking
 🔹 LEFT JOIN vs NOT EXISTS — performance matters
 🔹 PySpark transformations — lazy vs action mindset
 🔹 Broadcast joins — when & why, not just how
 🔹 GroupBy & aggregation — alias, optimization follow-ups
 🔹 End-to-end pipeline design — API → Raw → Transform → Serve
 🔹 SCD Type 1 vs Type 2 — MERGE / UPSERT logic
 🔹 ADF vs Databricks — orchestration vs transformation
 🔹 Incremental data loads — metadata tracking, Autoloader
 🔹 Real production thinking — performance tuning & cost awareness
👉 What interviewers really want:
 • Clear explanation of why, not just what
 • Real-world trade-offs
 • Incremental & scalable design
 • Confidence in fundamentals
If you’re preparing for Deloitte / Big4 / Product-based data roles, remember this 👇

author: Gunja Singh
headline: Data Engineer | 5+ Years Experience | ETL, Big Data, Cloud (AWS | Azure | GCP) | SQL | Python | Spark
text:
🚨 Data Engineers: These interview questions are NOT about Spark or SQL…
 They’re about how your brain works under pressure.
I learned this the hard way 👇
In recent interviews, I realized most rejections don’t happen because you don’t know tools…
 They happen because you don’t understand what’s happening under the hood.
Here are some tricky questions that separate real Data Engineers from resume engineers:
🧠 1. Same Spark job + same input → different output. Why?
 → Non-deterministic functions, partitioning, shuffle behavior, floating-point precision.
⚡ 2. Why is COUNT(*) faster than COUNT(column)?
 → Column scans + NULL handling vs metadata optimization.
🐌 3. Can increasing partitions make Spark slower?
 → Yes. Too many partitions = scheduler overhead + shuffle explosion.
🧩 4. Pipeline is idempotent, still duplicates appear. How?
 → Wrong business key, late data, race conditions, bad MERGE logic.
🔥 5. Kafka guarantees ordering… then why do events arrive out of order?
 → Ordering is only within a partition, not across them.
📦 6. Why is SELECT * dangerous in data lakes?
 → Breaks column pruning, increases I/O, memory, and network cost.
🧱 7. What is data skew… in simple words?
 → One worker doing 99% of the work while others wait.
If you’re a 0–5 year Data Engineer in 2026, prepare like this:
 Join 1000+ learners who landed offers at TCS, Deloitte, Infosys, and more —
 not by luck, but by mastering real data engineering scenarios.
 👉 Data Engineer Interview Mega Pack 👉 https://lnkd.in/gBfGiUpf

 👉 Top 100 Real Data Engineer Questions (1–4 Years Experience) 👉 https://lnkd.in/g_2VtMR4
💡 Bonus truth:
 You cannot build a system that is…
❌ Infinitely scalable
 ❌ Strictly ordered
 ❌ Exactly-once
 ❌ Real-time
 ❌ Cheap
…at the same time.
Trade-offs are the real job.
If you’re preparing for Data Engineer interviews in 2026, focus on:
✔️ Execution plans
 ✔️ Distributed system behavior
 ✔️ Failure scenarios
 ✔️ Data correctness
 ✔️ Performance trade-offs
Not just syntax.

author: Rohit Honde
headline: Senior Data Engineer @ ZS | Ex-Cognizant | Databricks | Data Factory| PySpark | Python | SQL | Azure | AWS
text:
“I thought I was ready for Data Engineering interviews… until these questions showed up.”

At mid–senior levels, interviews don’t test tools — they test systems thinking, scalability, and reliability.

Here are 10 Data Engineering questions that separate pipeline builders from platform engineers:

1️⃣ How would you design a data platform that supports both real-time analytics and historical reporting without duplicating logic?
 2️⃣ How do you ensure exactly-once or effectively-once processing in distributed data pipelines?
 3️⃣ How do you design pipelines to handle backfills without impacting ongoing production workloads?
 4️⃣ How do you version datasets and pipelines to support reproducibility and rollback?
 5️⃣ How would you design data partitioning strategies to balance performance and cost at scale?
 6️⃣ How do you handle upstream source failures without cascading impact on downstream systems?
 7️⃣ How do you design pipelines to support GDPR / data deletion requests across multiple layers?
 8️⃣ How do you decide what transformations belong in ingestion vs transformation layers — and why?
 9️⃣ How do you monitor data freshness, completeness, and accuracy in near real-time?
 🔟 Describe a time when your pipeline worked technically but failed the business — what went wrong and what changed?

If your preparation is only about tools and syntax, interviews will expose the gap.

Strong data engineers think in design, trade-offs, and failure scenarios.

 Which of these would you expect in your next interview?

headline: Data & AI @Barclays | Data Engineer | Ex-EY | Python | AWS| Azure | Spark| HIVE | PySpark | Databricks
text:
🚀 Data Engineer Interview Questions I Faced Recently

While giving interviews recently, I noticed a clear pattern in the types of questions being asked for Data Engineer roles — especially around real-world data platform design and production scenarios.

Here are a few that stood out 👇

Here are a few that stood out 👇
🔹 1. How do you design a scalable data pipeline from source to analytics?
 Ingestion strategy (batch vs streaming)
 Storage design (bronze/silver/gold, partitioning)
 Transformation approach (Spark, SQL, DLT)
 Data quality enforcement
 Monitoring and failure recovery

🔹 2. How do you handle incremental data efficiently?
 CDC patterns
 Delta Lake Change Data Feed (CDF)
 Watermarking and idempotent pipelines
 Late-arriving data handling

🔹 3. How do you optimize Spark jobs for performance?

 Partitioning vs bucketing
 Broadcast joins
 Shuffle optimization
 Adaptive Query Execution
 File size management

🔹 4. How do you ensure data quality and reliability in production?

 Data validation frameworks
 Schema enforcement
 Expectation checks (DLT, Great Expectations)
 Monitoring, alerting, and SLA design

🔹 5. How do you manage schema evolution and breaking changes?

 Schema enforcement vs evolution
 Backward/forward compatibility
 Versioning strategies
 Downstream impact management

💡 Key takeaway:
 Most interviews today test your ability to design resilient, scalable, and cost-efficient data systems — not just write SQL or Spark code.

If you’re preparing for data engineering interviews, focus on:
 ✅ Architecture thinking
 ✅ Production trade-offs
 ✅ Failure scenarios
 ✅ Performance tuning
 ✅ Data governance
